passages.heading: Day 1 — Notice
passages.text:
public defense lives in your body before it lives in your calendar. Welcome to day one of *Public Defender*. Everything this week is built on a single move — noticing what is already happening inside you before trying to change it.

Most people try to solve public defense with better planning. It doesn't work because public defense is a nervous-system state, not a scheduling problem. Today we locate where in the body it actually sits.

The one-line you'll carry today: **public defense lives in your body before it lives in your calendar.**

Don't try to make this profound. The whole point of a seven-day arc is that small, honest moves — done in a real body on a real Tuesday — outperform any amount of philosophy. Read the practice once, do it once, and let the rest of the day carry it for you.

passages.heading: Day 2 — Breathe
passages.text:
The exhale is the off-switch. Day 2 of *Public Defender*. Today we build directly on what yesterday opened.

A long exhale down-regulates the vagus nerve faster than any thought can. Under public defense, breath shortens. We reverse it deliberately.

The one-line you'll carry today: **The exhale is the off-switch.**

Don't try to make this profound. The whole point of a seven-day arc is that small, honest moves — done in a real body on a real Tuesday — outperform any amount of philosophy. Read the practice once, do it once, and let the rest of the day carry it for you.

passages.heading: Locate the Charge
passages.text:
1. Sit. Close your eyes.
2. Name the situation of nature out loud in one sentence.
3. Scan the body top to bottom. Where does the sensation live? Jaw? Chest? Belly?
4. Rest attention there for 60 seconds. Don't fix it. Meet it.

passages.heading: 4-8 Breath
passages.text:
Inhale 4 counts through the nose.
Exhale 8 counts through slightly pursed lips.
Repeat for 10 rounds.
Use this in the first 90 seconds of any nature spike.

passages.heading: Wide-Angle Attention
passages.text:
1. Close eyes. Hear the furthest sound you can.
2. Feel the weight of your body on the chair.
3. Feel the air on your skin.
4. Now, from this wider place, look at nature again. It shrinks.

passages.heading: Precise Naming
passages.text:
1. Feel the current wave of nature.
2. Ask: is it fear, grief, anger, shame, or overwhelm?
3. Get more specific: is it fear of being seen, fear of failing, fear of being alone?
4. Say the precise name out loud. Notice what changes.

passages.heading: Shake It Off
passages.text:
1. Stand up.
2. Shake hands, arms, legs, whole body for 90 seconds. Loose.
3. Then still. Feel the aliveness under the skin.
4. Sit and notice how nature has changed.

passages.heading: Build Your Anchor
passages.text:
1. Pick one physical gesture (hand on chest, thumb & finger together, feet firmly planted).
2. Sit calmly and combine it with 3 slow breaths.
3. Repeat 5 times so the pairing sets.
4. Use it once today in real life.

passages.heading: Design Your Minimum
passages.text:
1. Of this week's practices, pick one that took under 3 minutes.
2. Attach it to something you already do daily (morning coffee, closing laptop).
3. Commit to 30 days of that pairing.
4. Write it on paper. Put it where you'll see it.

passages.heading: Attention Audit
passages.text:
1. For one waking hour, log every device pickup.
2. Beside each, write: cue, duration, aftermath.
3. Look for the pattern that surprises you.
4. Name the biggest leak in one word.

passages.heading: One-Tab Hour
passages.text:
1. Pick one 60-minute block today.
2. One tab. One task. Phone in another room.
3. When distraction rises, note it on paper, return.
4. End: notice quality difference.

passages.heading: 10 Breaths
passages.text:
1. Sit or stand.
2. Count 10 breaths in and out, only.
3. Lose count? Restart. No punishment.
4. Use before every silence session for the rest of the week.

passages.heading: Sit With Nothing
passages.text:
1. Sit for 5 minutes with no input. No music. No phone.
2. Watch what the mind does at minute 2 and 4.
3. Do not resolve. Notice.
4. Return to silence refreshed.

passages.heading: Sleep Contract
passages.text:
1. Choose a lights-out time you can hold 5 nights in a row.
2. 60 minutes before: no work, no fast content.
3. 30 minutes before: dim lights.
4. Track it. Sleep is training.

passages.heading: Design The Field
passages.text:
1. Clear one surface entirely.
2. Put one object of intent on it (book, note, image).
3. Remove one visible distraction.
4. Work from this field tomorrow morning.

passages.heading: Stop At 90%
passages.text:
1. In your next work block, set a timer for 25 minutes.
2. Stop when it rings, even if you're mid-sentence.
3. Walk for 5 minutes.
4. Return with fuller attention.

passages.heading: Meet The Ache
passages.text:
1. Sit quietly. Hand on chest.
2. Bring thanks to mind.
3. Feel the physical sensation, not the story.
4. Say inside: "I'm here. You can be here too."

passages.heading: Find The Origin
passages.text:
1. Ask: "When did I first feel exactly this?"
2. Wait. Don't force it.
3. When something arises, write one line about it.
4. Notice the age of thanks.

passages.heading: Offer It Up
passages.text:
1. Sit. Hand on heart.
2. Bring the person or situation of thanks to mind.
3. Whisper: "For your wellbeing, not mine."
4. Repeat 21 times.

passages.heading: One Clean Sentence
passages.text:
1. Identify the thanks situation where a limit is overdue.
2. Write the sentence, no adjectives.
3. Read it aloud to the mirror.
4. Deliver it before Friday.

passages.heading: Release Ritual
passages.text:
1. Sit. Bring the person or self to mind.
2. Say: "I am not agreeing. I am putting this down."
3. Physically open your hands.
4. Breathe out longer than in.

passages.heading: Three Absences
passages.text:
1. Name three things in your life that, if gone tomorrow, you would grieve.
2. Name them out loud.
3. Feel the pull of them, not the concept.
4. Rest there.

passages.heading: Signature Prayer
passages.text:
1. Write a 3-line prayer about thanks.
2. Read it aloud.
3. Say it once each morning for 30 days.
4. Notice what changes in you, not in the situation.
